sample_unit: clinical cases (70 diagnostic, 30 management; 1,020 rubric criteria)

links.outcome: Calibration of self-reported system confidence against diagnostic accuracy (Brier score)
links.effect: Self-reported confidence was generally high, and all systems were systematically overconfident; the lowest Brier score was 0.203 (Claude Fable 5).
links.quote: Self-reported system confidence was generally high and diagnostic calibration analyses showed systematic overconfidence for all systems, with the lowest Brier score of 0.203 (Claude Fable 5).

links.outcome: Diagnostic top-1 and top-3 accuracy on rheumatology cases; severity of errors
links.effect: Top-1 accuracy peaked at 57.1% (GPT-5.6 Sol) and top-3 at 67.1% (Claude Fable 5). Potentially severe errors, mostly omissions, occurred with all systems.
links.quote: Diagnostic top-1 accuracy reached 57.1% (GPT-5.6 Sol), while top-3 accuracy reached 67.1% (Claude Fable 5).

unlisted_practices: Rubric-based, specialist-validated benchmark with an LLM-judge panel for evaluating open-ended clinical LLM responses
Comparison of thorough versus standard prompting on management-case performance

screen.reason: The study develops and applies a specialist-validated benchmark (RheumBench) to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy, management, calibration, and potential harm of several LLMs and clinical RAG systems in rheumatology.
